record_type_quote: Recently, a genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified three new susceptibility loci for PACG, including rs11024102 in PLEKHA7, rs3753841 in COL11A1, and rs1015213 in PCMTD1-ST18 [14]. However, the mechanism of these genes in PACG pathogenesis is unclear, and the biological plausibility is absent. We hypothesized that PLEKHA7, COL11A1, and PCMTD1-ST18 might contribute to PACG by influencing ocular biometry. Thus, in this study, we attempted to replicate the association between these three loci with primary angle closure (PAC) instead of PACG to investigate whether the SNPs of these three genes are associated with ocular biometry.

targets.title: Genome-wide association analyses identify three new susceptibility loci for primary angle closure glaucoma.

targets.outcome_quote: Our results were not in line with Vithana et al.'s report [14] that reported the three loci susceptible for PACG by a GWAS study with a two-stage strategy.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit disagreement with the GWAS association results. Authors note low statistical power but affirm their sample is reasonable to detect a biologically meaningful association; they do not declare this attempt incapable of testing the claim.

reasoning: Independent Han Chinese case-control sample re-tests the three GWAS loci using an earlier disease phenotype. Three loci from one original paper count as one target. Day et al. is cited as a related genotype-phenotype comparison in discussion, not identified as the finding this study set out to re-test.
